newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Sun-and-sand Algarve set for bumper summer.
newsitem.headline: Sun-and-sand Algarve set for bumper summer.

text.p: Sun-and-sand tourism in the Algarve region of southern Portugal is set for a bumper summer as British tourists, the main source of revenue, take advantage of a strong pound, a senior tourism official said on Wednesday.

"The stronger pound against the escudo is good news not only for this year, but for next year as well," Eliderico Viegas, head of the Association of Hotels and Tourism Businesses of the Algarve (AHETA), told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"The rise in the pound is not just boosting demand for holidays, but is also leading to increased interest by the British in holiday homes and investment projects, notably in construction," he added.
Tourism in the Algarve brings in some eight million visitors and generates 600 billion escudos ($3.45 billion) in revenue a year, about 60 percent of Portugal's total tourism receipts.
The region has long stretches of sandy beach, many golf courses and a well-developed tourist infrastructure ranging from five-star hotels to basic self-catering apartments.

Viegas said he expected the number of foreign visitors to the Algarve to remain about the same this summer as last year as hotels were always heavily booked during the high season, but he expected the British to spend more during their holidays.
Demand for holidays in the Algarve would improve in the medium and low seasons after the summer, compared with 1996.
The average occupation rate per room in the Algarve was 73.9 percent in May, 6.6 percentage points more than in May last year, AHETA figures showed.
The Portuguese, benefiting from an improving economy, occupied five percent of hotel rooms in May, up from 4.2 percent in the same period last year.

The number of passengers travelling through the Algarve's main airport at Faro rose by 40,829 or 10.9 percent, compared with May last year. British, Dutch and Scandinavian passengers accounted for most of the increase.
Demand for golfing holidays exceeded supply and several projects to build new courses were being discussed, Viegas said.
The number of golf rounds in the Algarve rose 3.5 percent to 3,339 in May, compared with May 1996.
Tourism, mainly from northern Europe and Spain, accounts for some seven percent of Portugal's Gross Domestic Product and ranks alongside textiles as the sector contributing most to national wealth.
